subject: Re: Acme Health — model fit + streaming UX follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health kickoff — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

- Discovery highlights: you’re building an internal clinical-summarization assistant (triage + summarize) with strict PII controls and a hard latency target of <= 300ms tail for the streaming UX.
- Primary risks you flagged: partial-output coherence (clients seeing truncated/garbled partial tokens), stop-sequence behaviors for clinical templates, and potential quality regressions vs. your current baseline model when we enable quantized variants.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood runs a focused model-fit evaluation against your sample prompt set (please send) — we’ll test 3 candidate model/quant combos and send a short benchmark (latency, token-level coherence, and stop-sequence fidelity).
2) Share benchmark + prompt set + recommended model profile by Thu (03/25).
3) Follow-up call to review results and align on Dedicated/Private SOW.

I’ve cc’d Jordan (model-fit lead) and Chloe (solutions) to run the evals and coordinate timelines. Please reply with the sample prompts and any additional constraints (max tokens, stop tokens, streaming cadence).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_proposed_evals_plan.docx]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health kickoff — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:

- Prompt set: attached (small slice of anonymized clinical notes + 10 target prompts). Please keep any outputs within our environment/public preview off.
- Latency: 95th percentile target is 300ms for end-to-end streaming responses (we understand that tokenization + network hops add overhead).
- Stop sequences: our templates rely on a hard "

<END>" stop token; partial-output must not emit this token mid-stream unless the model finished the segment. We’ve seen cases where partial decoding shows fragments of the stop token and then final output gets cut.
- Success criteria for the eval: parity or improvement in clinical summary accuracy (measured by our annotation set), and maintain streaming coherence at the 95th latency target.

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json. Procurement is on cc and will need the benchmark + SOW for internal approvals.

Cheers,
Alex Turner
Director of AI Products, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.json]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health kickoff — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks for the prompt set. We ran an initial pass across two model families (open-llama-70b-int8, and rdx-13b-q4f) with default streaming client and a synthetic network hop to approximate your 95ms edge. Preliminary notes below (summary; detailed report attached):

- open-llama-70b-int8: highest quality on clinical coherence (annotation F1 delta +3.1% vs your baseline) but 95th P95 streaming latency ~420ms in our infra with default batching — improves to ~310ms with aggressive micro-batching and optimized KV cache pinning (config we can provide). Partial-output coherence was strong; stop tokens respected on 97% of cases but we saw fragmented stop token substrings on 3 examples.
- rdx-13b-q4f: P95 latency ~280ms with our optimized runtime and lower cost per token. However, we observed a small quality regression on rare entity disambiguation cases (F1 delta -1.8%). Stop-sequence behavior was mechanically faithful but partial-output sometimes produced trailing ellipses that confused client-side renderers.

Files attached: redwood_streaming_benchmark_summary.pdf (quick charts), and the config snippet we used. Next steps I propose:
1) Run a gated eval with your annotation set (if you can provide) for exact metrics.
2) Run a streaming-focused stability test that forces stop-sequence edge cases (we’ll produce a failing-case log).
3) If you want the <300ms P95 for the larger model, we should try Dedicated with pinned KV cache + micro-batching; I’ll scope cost delta for that.

Sharing the quick benchmark now: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/reports/acme_streaming_benchmark_20260324.pdf

-Jordan
Jordan Blake | Principal ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_benchmark_streaming_report.pdf]

---
On Thu, Mar 19, 2026 at 09:04, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:
> (see above)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health kickoff — post-call recap & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the quick pass. A few follow-ups after skimming the benchmark:

- The partial-output fragmentation you mentioned is concerning. I pasted a short example we saw in prod (anonymized):

  Client stream chunk: "...the patient was diagnosed with acute resp"
  Next chunk: "atory failure<EN"
  Final output: "atory failure

<END>"

The client rendered the mid-stream fragment ("resp") as a standalone token and that caused an incorrect highlight in our UI. We need streaming semantics that avoid exposing fragmentary tokens or provide clearer token-boundary guarantees.

- Also curious about recommended stop-token handling for clinical templates — should we post-process streams client-side to suppress partial stop-substrings, or is there a way to configure the runtime to avoid emitting fragments?

Procurement: when Jordan has a final benchmark + SOW, please share so we can start approvals.

-Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health kickoff — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great example, thank you. Plan to address the fragmentation and stop-token concerns:

1) Technical approach: Jordan will run a focused streaming-stability test that instruments token emission boundaries and surface a short failing-case log (we’ll include exact byte/granularity info). We can combine two mitigations: a) runtime-level atomic token flushing for stop-token suffixes, and b) a client-side sanitization snippet to suppress rendering of partial stop-substrings until token commit. We’ll include both options in the report.
2) Eval plan: we’ll run the gated eval against your annotation set (please share) and produce a short report next Tue (03/30). Attached is the proposed eval plan and the benchmark PDF for reference.
3) Procurement/SOW: Chloe — can you prepare a short SOW + estimated cost delta for Dedicated (pinned KV cache) vs Hosted (optimized micro-batching) so Alex’s procurement team has numbers to review.

Proposed follow-up: 30 min review call on Tue 03/30 10:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks — we’ll aim to surface the failing-case list and recommended runtime config by the end of next week.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: acme_proposed_evals_plan.docx, redwood_benchmark_streaming_report.pdf]
